recorded_by: claude (retrospective reconstruction from commit messages - no contemporaneous ledger was kept for this PR)
trigger: a management-group-confined caller calls preview_scope_targets or POST /api/v1/scope/preview
policy_floor: routed-concerns.md's authorize_list_read row: every new list/fan-out read of per-agent data MUST use the admit-then-filter chokepoint, never a bare global require_permission
summary: preview_scope_targets (and its new REST v1 twin) gated on a bare Infrastructure:Read perm_fn/permission check and evaluated the expression against the UNFILTERED agent snapshot - a management-group-confined caller could see every connected agent's match, not just their own visible set. Fixed both surfaces to gate via fleet_read_fn_/fleet_read_fn and narrow the candidate agent list to gate.scope.

trigger: a management-group-confined caller with a real but narrower Inventory:Read grant calls create_result_set_from_inventory_query or its REST twin
policy_floor: routed-concerns.md's authorize_list_read row (same class as b2-1)
summary: Same confinement gap as b2-1: gated on a bare perm_fn(Inventory, Read), evaluated over every agent's inventory records fleet-wide. Could enumerate device-identity + inventory-attribute correlation outside the caller's visible set. Fixed via fleet_read_fn_/fleet_read_fn, same pattern as GET /api/v1/inventory/software.

trigger: a caller sends a non-object element in conditions[], or a field with the wrong JSON type, to create_result_set_from_inventory_query
summary: nlohmann::json::type_error: .value(key, default) throws on a type mismatch rather than coercing (MCP input-schema validation is approval-gated only, so this reached the loop directly). Uncaught exception crash class on both transports. Fixed with explicit type checks, returning 400/kInvalidParams instead.

trigger: REST's from-inventory-query call site invokes an unwired fleet_read_fn (test fixture had never wired one, since the route used to call perm_fn)
summary: b2-2's fix was missing the null-guard every other fleet_read_fn call site has - calling an unwired fleet_read_fn throws std::bad_function_call, breaking 2 pre-existing tests. A prior "0 failures" claim only held because the relevant tests are Postgres-gated and were silently skipped in a no-DSN run. Fixed by adding the guard and wiring a fake fleet_read_fn in the test harness.

trigger: the new conditions-validation regression tests run against a fixture with no inventory_store wired
policy_floor: a false-green test offered as closure evidence for a blocking finding
summary: b2-3's new tests couldn't reach the code under test - store-availability checks ran before the conditions-validation loop, so both hit an early store-unavailable branch instead. Reordered validation ahead of store checks on both MCP and REST (also better production behavior).

trigger: a reader of the 2 comments/2 doc rows claiming create_result_set_from_inventory_query/preview_scope_targets have no per-device/service-tag scoping, after b2-1/b2-2 landed
summary: Comments/docs contradicted code per CLAUDE.md rule 3 (truth, not wording-only). Updated to state the real remaining gap: service-scoped tokens are confined, not hard-denied, unlike this tool's 8 non-dispatch siblings - tracked #4307.

trigger: an auditor filters ResultSet target/id for a denial produced by MCP's shared rs_load_owned helper across all 12 result-set tools
summary: rs_load_owned only emitted a generic mcp_audit call (id in free text) where REST's twin uses a structured audit_fn call. Added the matching structured call alongside.

trigger: n/a - bundle of 3 findings confirmed pre-existing in REST's shared run_async/ResultSetStore::members()
adjudication_rationale: pre-existing REST behavior this batch mirrors rather than worsens in kind, per the established Batch B1 UP-1/UP-3 precedent
waiver_rationale: explicit direction to file rather than fix, matching the established policy for this exact category
summary: Bundle: dishonest retry_after_ms after a real dispatch already fired; reevaluate_result_set broadcasting fleet-wide on a deleted parent; from-inventory-query's parent-narrowing silently dropping members on a transient error. All confirmed pre-existing, not introduced by this branch. NOTE: partially superseded at pass_ordinal 5 (b2-9) once one of these mechanisms was found to be MCP-new, not REST-mirrored after all.

trigger: rs_run_async's dispatch throws, or create_pending returns a DbError after sent>0/set_agents_targeted already called
summary: rs_run_async answered retry_after_ms:5000 after a real dispatch had already fired, contradicting these tools' own "NEVER re-send" contract. Verified this mechanism is MCP-new code, not REST-mirrored (REST's rs_err is structurally incapable of emitting a retry hint - checked via all 37 call sites), correcting b2-8's framing for this specific mechanism. Both branches now answer kInternalError with no retry hint.

trigger: a caller sends a large conditions[] array with combine="any" to create_result_set_from_inventory_query
summary: No size cap on conditions[] - O(conditions x records), combine="any"'s short-circuit trivially defeated, one request could pin a shared httplib worker indefinitely. Added kMaxInventoryConditions (500) at both transports plus a defense-in-depth backstop inside evaluate_inventory() itself.

trigger: reevaluate_result_set's tar_query branch runs against a result set whose sql was minted via the uncapped create_result_set with a fabricated tar_query source_kind
summary: reevaluate_result_set's tar_query branch only checked sql.empty(), not the 100000-byte cap, letting an oversized SQL payload smuggle past the dedicated 200 KiB body cap and dispatch fleet-wide on re-eval. Re-applied the same cap create_result_set_from_tar_query enforces.

trigger: a caller sends a wrong-typed combine/name (from-inventory-query) or include_empty (from-tar-query) argument
summary: Same .value(key, default) type-error crash class as b2-3, on 3 more parameters across both transports. Added explicit type checks; also reordered from-inventory-query's parent_id validation ahead of the store-availability check.

trigger: the POST /api/v1/inventory/evaluate route (a 3rd, pre-existing caller of evaluate_inventory() this PR never intended to touch) receives an oversized conditions[] request
summary: kMaxInventoryConditions was enforced on both result-set producers but not this pre-existing third caller. An oversized request silently hit the library-level backstop and returned 200 {"data":[]} instead of being rejected - a wrong-result-presented-as-correct regression. Added the same 400 pre-check.

policy_floor: routed-concerns.md's authorize_list_read row (same class as b2-1/b2-2)
summary: This route retained the exact CWE-862 confinement gap b2-1/b2-2 fixed for its two siblings on the same evaluate_inventory() call chain - the earlier fix diff touched this exact handler (adding the DoS cap) but applied only the DoS half, missing the confinement half. Switched to fleet_read_fn; also fixed the same unguarded .get<std::string>() type-confusion the sibling routes already got.

trigger: any caller runs preview_scope_targets/POST /api/v1/scope/preview with an ostype condition
summary: scope_preview.cpp populated attrs["os"] instead of the DSL's canonical "ostype" attribute - the entire tool's purpose is "show what a real dispatch would target before committing", and it was silently wrong: ostype=="linux" always resolved unset (matched_count silently 0), ostype!="linux" resolved true for EVERY agent. A pre-existing test locked the wrong dialect in. Fixed the resolver key and the test; added a regression test pinning the known, separately-tracked (#4307) NOT-inversion-on-an-unresolved-atom behavior.

policy_floor: a false-green test offered as closure evidence for a blocking finding
summary: "Suite green" was cited as closure evidence, but no test exercised either branch check-mcp-retry-hints.py cannot lexically detect (a catch block; a bare DbError comparison with no call-site guard prefix). Added two integration tests actually triggering a throwing dispatch_fn and a real post-dispatch DbError (schema drop), pinning the absence of retry_after_ms on both paths.
